section: 2. reward models: turning rankings into a score
text: Labellers rank K sampled responses to a prompt (InstructGPT used K = 4 to 9), which gives K(K−1)/2 comparisons, and the model is trained on the Bradley-Terry objective: the probability that people prefer y w over y l is modelled as σ(r(x, y w ) − r(x, y l )), and the loss maximises it. loss(θ) = − 1/(K choose 2) · E (x, y w , y l ) [ log σ( r θ (x, y w ) − r θ (x, y l ) ) ] r θ (x, y) the reward model's scalar for prompt x and response y y w , y l the preferred ("winning") and the other response of one comparison σ the logistic function; only the difference of two rewards matters, so a reward has no absolute zero K responses ranked per prompt InstructGPT's Eq.

section: 3. rl against a reward: ppo and grpo in brief
text: GRPO removes the per-response length normalisation that lets long wrong answers off lightly and the standard-deviation division that over-weights too-easy and too-hard prompts ( arXiv 2503.20783 ); DAPO decouples the clip range (clip-higher), drops groups with no spread (dynamic sampling), averages over tokens and shapes overlong answers ( arXiv 2503.14476 ); GSPO clips one length-normalised ratio per sequence, for stability on long answers and mixture-of-experts models ( arXiv 2507.18071 ); CISPO , from MiniMax-M1, "clips importance sampling weights rather than token updates" ( arXiv 2506.13585 ).
